chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Sulayman, who said: We were narrated by Ali ibn Abi Khulays, who said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Mutahhir narrated to me, who said: I wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him):

That a man narrated from your forefathers (peace be upon them) that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not increase in prayer during the month of Ramadan beyond what he used to pray on other days.

So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'He lied, may Allah expose his mouth. Pray twenty rak'ahs every night of the month of Ramadan until the twentieth of the month, and pray on the night of the twenty-first one hundred rak'ahs, and pray on the night of the twenty-third one hundred rak'ahs, and pray in each of the last ten nights thirty rak'ahs.'
ai.seo_question: What is the specific number of night prayer rak'ahs prescribed in Ramadan according to Imam al-Hadi (AS)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Hadi (peace be upon him) clarifies the specific structure of Tarawih prayers, prescribing twenty rak'ahs for the first twenty nights and increasing to one hundred rak'ahs on the 21st and 23rd nights, with thirty for the final ten nights. This narration is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for establishing the variable count of night prayers during Ramadan, distinguishing it from the fixed practices of other months. It highlights the emphasis on spiritual devotion during the latter part of the month, particularly the odd nights associated with Laylat al-Qadr.
